title: Shopping Cart
statement:
Tony is visiting a supermarket to buy **Z** cans of coke. The supermarket offers only two types of packs:

- A pack of **2 cans** costs **X** dollars.
- A pack of **4 cans** costs **Y** dollars.

Tony can purchase any number of these packs. He is allowed to buy **more than Z cans** if necessary, but he cannot buy individual cans.

For each test case, determine the **minimum total cost** required to purchase **at least Z cans**.

### Input Format
- The first line contains an integer **T**, the number of test cases.
- Each of the next **T** lines contains three space-separated integers: **X**, **Y**, and **Z**.

### Output Format
- For each test case, print a single integer representing the minimum total cost on a new line.

examples.explanation:
Test Case 1:
X = 5, Y = 10, Z = 10
• Five 2-packs → 10 cans → Cost = 25
• Two 4-packs + One 2-pack → 10 cans → Cost = 25
• Three 4-packs → 12 cans → Cost = 30
Minimum cost = 25.

Test Case 2:
X = 5, Y = 8, Z = 10
• Five 2-packs → 10 cans → Cost = 25
• Two 4-packs + One 2-pack → 10 cans → Cost = 21
• Three 4-packs → 12 cans → Cost = 24
Minimum cost = 21.

Test Case 3:
X = 4, Y = 7, Z = 5
• Three 2-packs → 6 cans → Cost = 12
• One 4-pack + One 2-pack → 6 cans → Cost = 11
• Two 4-packs → 8 cans → Cost = 14
Minimum cost = 11.

hints: Check if buying 4-packs is cheaper per can than buying 2-packs (i.e. Y < 2 * X).
If Y >= 2 * X, buy ceil(Z / 2) two-packs.
If Y < 2 * X, buy Z // 4 four-packs and resolve remainder cans efficiently.
discussion: Compare the cost of full 4-packs and optimal combinations for remaining cans.
